# Introduction {.unnumbered}

These notes accompany the NGS Data Analysis module.  
They focus on the **`SummarizedExperiment`** family of R/Bioconductor objects — the standard container for virtually every modern high-throughput sequencing analysis pipeline.

## Why a dedicated container?

NGS experiments produce at least **three interconnected tables** that must always stay in sync:

| Table | Rows | Columns | Contains |
|-------|------|---------|----------|
| Count / assay matrix | Genes/features | Samples | Raw counts, TPM, FPKM… |
| Sample metadata | Samples | Attributes | Condition, batch, sex… |
| Feature metadata | Genes/features | Attributes | Gene name, chromosome, GC%… |

Keeping these three tables aligned by hand is error-prone.  
`SummarizedExperiment` **binds** them into one object and guarantees they never go out of sync.

## The SummarizedExperiment family

```
SummarizedExperiment (SE)
└── RangedSummarizedExperiment (RSE)   ← what you saw in class
    ├── DESeqDataSet         (DESeq2)
    ├── SingleCellExperiment (scRNA-seq)
    └── …and many more
```

`RangedSummarizedExperiment` **adds genomic coordinates** (a `GRanges` object) to each row/feature, enabling range-based operations.

## Package installation

```r
# Install from Bioconductor
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install("SummarizedExperiment")

# Also very useful
BiocManager::install(c("GenomicRanges", "DESeq2", "tximeta"))
```

## How to use these notes

Each chapter builds on the previous one:

1. **Structure** — visual anatomy of an RSE object
2. **Access & Manipulation** — how to get data in and out
3. **Workflow** — from raw counts to a ready-to-analyse RSE
